These days in nature, black holes are formed from collapsed stars. However, in the early days of the universe, it's thought that the universe was dense enough for primordial black holes to form. Those could have come in nearly any size. Stellar black holes, though massive, can still shrink in mass from Hawking radiation. This means that Earth-mass black holes could naturally be hanging around.

Regardless of how it formed, black holes can theoretically form from any mass. The only key is that the mass has to be in an area small enough. The minimum radius of such an area is called the Schwarzschild radius. Compress the Earth below about 9 millimeters and you have an Earth-mass black hole. (Of course you first have to get through eletrostatic repulsion, degeneracy pressures, etc. And if you can't, you do get the explosion you're thinking of. But anything is possible if you work hard and put your mind to it!)

Type 1 - Informative content & new articles.

Type 2 - Text content, self posts, questions, etc

Type 3 - Non serious, informal, funny content
